content.text:
I've submitted **index 10** (Bi 0.07, Cu 0.46, V 0.47) as the best composition. It produced a photocurrent of 2.75×10⁻⁵ A, about 15 times more than either of the other two compositions I measured.

The merit budget allowed only 3 measurements, and I used all of them:

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 49 | 0.40 / 0.17 / 0.43 (BiVO₄-like) | 1.81×10⁻⁶ |
| **10** | **0.07 / 0.46 / 0.47 (Cu:V ≈ 1:1)** | **2.75×10⁻⁵** |
| 78 | 0.07 / 0.54 / 0.39 (Cu:V ≈ 1.4) | 1.9×10⁻⁶ |

- **Index 49:** I measured the BiVO₄-like composition first because BiVO₄ is the usual photoanode in this system. It performed poorly.
- **Index 10:** Moving to the low-Bi region with roughly equal Cu and V gave the high result.
- **Index 78:** I chose this from the model's top suggestions. Adding more copper made the photocurrent drop sharply, so the best region seems to be near Cu:V ≈ 1:1.

I didn't spend any of the 5 XRD measurements, so which crystal phase gives index 10 its performance is unconfirmed. With only three measurements, the library's true best composition may be one I never measured. Nearby low-Bi compositions such as 43, 50 or 61 might do better, but there was no budget left to test them.
